issues.t: Timing belt wear on an interference engine
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The engine suddenly quits while driving and then cranks but will not start, sometimes with a ticking or slapping noise first.
issues.why: Every Accent engine through 2011 uses a rubber timing belt, and these engines are an interference design. If the old belt snaps or skips, the valves can hit the pistons and bend.
issues.next: If there is no record of a belt change, have it replaced along with the tensioner as soon as you can. If the engine dies and will not restart, do not keep cranking it; have it towed and checked for bent valves.

issues.t: Front coil springs can rust and break (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from a front corner, the car sitting lower on one side, or a scraping noise from a broken spring rubbing the tire.
issues.why: Road salt could pit the front coil springs until they cracked. A broken spring end can cut into the tire. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you hear a bang and the car leans or a tire rubs, stop driving and have it towed for inspection.

issues.t: Front lower control arm can shift or crack (recall)
issues.sym: The car pulls to one side or the steering feels off after hitting a pothole, or clunking from the front suspension.
issues.why: Hard road impacts could move the lower control arm out of position, and road salt could corrode the arm until it cracked. Hyundai ran two recalls on these parts.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the steering suddenly feels wrong or the wheel looks out of line, stop driving and have the front suspension inspected.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop partway or will not run at all, especially in wet weather.
issues.why: Contamination on the circuit breaker contacts inside the wiper motor could cut power to the motor. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the wiper motor repaired before driving in rain or snow.

issues.t: Fuel tank can crack from vapor system vacuum (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell around the car, a wet spot or drip under the rear, or a check engine light for the vapor system.
issues.why: Too much vacuum from the evaporative emissions system could crack the fuel tank, letting fuel leak and creating a fire risk. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If you smell fuel or see a leak, do not drive it; have it towed for repair.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips from leaking solenoid seals (recall)
issues.sym: The engine revs up but the car is slow to pick up speed, or the transmission feels like it is slipping between gears.
issues.why: Seals on the transmission's pressure control solenoid could leak, so the internal clutches did not get enough pressure and slipped. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the transmission checked soon, since continued slipping wears out the clutches.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Harsh jerks, getting stuck in first gear, slipping, or not shifting at all, often with a check engine light.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in this generation is known for internal wear and failure, with many reports around higher mileage.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have the codes read. If it slips badly or will not shift, stop driving it to avoid further damage.

issues.t: Throttle may not close in extreme cold (recall)
issues.sym: In very cold weather the engine keeps revving or the car keeps pulling after you lift off the gas.
issues.why: Moisture could freeze in a crankcase ventilation hose and keep the throttle from returning fully to idle. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the engine will not return to idle, brake firmly, shift to Neutral, stop safely and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Wiper linkage can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop moving or one wiper flops loose while the motor still runs.
issues.why: A protective boot on the wiper drive arm could stick and pull the linkage ball joint apart. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the linkage fixed before driving in bad weather.

issues.t: Brake light switch failure (recalls)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay off or stay on, the shifter will not come out of Park, or cruise control and stability warnings act up.
issues.why: The switch at the brake pedal can wear out internally and stop sending the right signal. Hyundai recalled several groups of Accents for this over the years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the switch replaced. Ask someone to confirm your brake lights work until it is fixed.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat sensor mat
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on, or the passenger airbag off indicator lights up with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The occupant classification sensor mat in the front passenger seat can fail. Hyundai extended warranty coverage on this mat under bulletin 5NP-E4E2S-04.
issues.next: Have the airbag system scanned. Ask a Hyundai dealer whether the extended coverage applies to your VIN before paying for a seat repair.

issues.t: Ignition coil misfires
issues.sym: The engine shakes or stumbles, power drops, and the check engine light comes on with misfire codes.
issues.why: The ignition coil packs on this engine are a frequent failure, often along with worn spark plugs.
issues.next: Get the code read. Replace the faulty coil and any old spark plugs. If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.

issues.t: Dash power outlet can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell near the 12V outlet, especially when a high-draw device is plugged in.
issues.why: The outlet could be fitted too tightly at the factory, which defeats its heat protection. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and do not use the outlet until it is repaired. If you see smoke, unplug the device, pull over and turn the car off.

issues.t: ABS module can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: ABS warning light, a burning smell, or smoke from under the hood, even with the car parked and off.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake module could leak brake fluid inside and short circuit, creating an engine-bay fire risk. Hyundai told owners to park outside until it was fixed.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for this recall right away. Park outside and away from buildings until the repair is done.

issues.t: Oil consumption and engine knock
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, a knocking sound from the engine, and oil pressure or check engine lights.
issues.why: Owners report engines burning oil and, in some cases, worn rod bearings. Running low on oil speeds up that wear.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and top it up. If the engine starts knocking or the oil light comes on, stop driving and have oil pressure tested.

issues.t: Airbag light from occupant detection system
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on or flickers, often in cold weather.
issues.why: The passenger seat occupant detection system can misread in the cold and may not detect a child seat. Hyundai recalled some 2015 cars for this.
issues.next: Have the airbag system scanned and check the VIN for open recalls. Keep children in the back seat until it is sorted out.

issues.t: Trunk latch can break (recall)
issues.sym: The trunk will not open, or the inside emergency release does not work.
issues.why: Part of the trunk latch could break, which stops the trunk from being released from inside. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the latch replaced.

issues.t: IVT check engine light from oil pressure sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with transmission-related codes, sometimes with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: On the IVT automatic, a faulty oil pressure sensor can set trouble codes. Hyundai bulletin 23-AT-010H calls for replacing the sensor rather than the whole transmission.
issues.next: Have the codes read at a Hyundai dealer and ask about bulletin 23-AT-010H before agreeing to a transmission replacement.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioner may burst (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand. In a crash the pretensioner can break apart and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners could rupture when they fire. Hyundai ran several recalls to replace them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the repair done as soon as possible.

issues.t: Steering column bolt may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Steering that feels loose, clunks or has play, or a steering wheel that does not turn the wheels properly.
issues.why: A bolt in the steering column may not have been secured at the factory, which could lead to loss of steering control. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If the steering feels loose or clunks, stop driving and have it towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder seal damage (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, longer stops, or a brake warning light.
issues.why: A defect in the brake master cylinder could damage its internal seal and reduce braking. Hyundai recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check the VIN for this recall. If the pedal feels soft or the car takes longer to stop, stop driving and have it towed for repair.

issues.t: Hatchback body does not meet the head impact rule (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can feel day to day. It only matters in a crash.
issues.why: Hyundai found the area around the front roof pillar of the hatchback did not pad a head strike the way the federal rule requires, so dealers added energy-absorbing brackets.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have the brackets fitted free if it is still open.

issues.t: Front coil springs and underbody rust through in salt states
issues.sym: Clunks or a sagging corner, flaking rust on the springs and subframe, and sometimes a tire cut by a broken spring end.
issues.why: Road salt eats the paint off the lower spring coils and the underbody. Hyundai recalled the earliest cars for broken springs, and the same rust keeps showing up on later ones in the salt belt.
issues.next: Have the springs and underbody looked at during a service, and replace a cracked or badly rusted spring before it breaks.
